   MINUTES
  MALIBU PUBLIC FACILITIES AUTHORITY MEETING
  SPECIAL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 6, 2023
  TELECONFERENCED – VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  1:00 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from
various locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Greenstein called the meeting to order at 1:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance:

  PRESENT: Chair Nancy Greenstein; and Commissioners Margaret Quińones-
  Perez, Bruce Silverstein, and Steve Uhring

  ALSO PRESENT: Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) Members Steve
  McClary, City Manager, City of Malibu (Malibu), and Dr. Kathryn Jeffery, Santa
  Monica College (SMC) Superintendent/President; Alexis Brown, Malibu Deputy
  City Manager; Donald Girard, SMC Senior Director of Government Relations and
  Institutional Relations; Chris Bonvenuto, SMC Vice President of Administration
  and Business Services; Charlie Yen, SMC Director of Facilities Planning; Alice
  Meyering, Associate Dean, SMC Malibu Campus; Scott Silverman, SMC
  Noncredit and External Programs Dean; Shari Davis, Project Manager, SMC
  Special Projects; Parker Davis, Malibu Media Technician; and Mary Linden,
  Malibu Executive Assistant

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Uhring moved, and Commissioner Quińones-Perez
  seconded a motion to approve the agenda. The question was called, and the
  motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Malibu Executive Assistant Linden reported that the agenda for the meeting was
  properly posted on August 30, 2023.

  None.

ITEM 2  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Commissioner Quińones-Perez moved, and Commissioner Uhring
  seconded a motion to approve the Consent Calendar. The question was

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following item:

  A.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended action: Approve minutes for the Malibu Public
  Facilities Authority meetings of October 13, 2022 and April 6, 2023.

ITEM 3  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 4  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Santa Monica College Malibu Campus Facilities Update
  Recommended Action: Receive an update on the ongoing activities related
  to the construction of the Santa Monica College (SMC) Malibu Campus.

  SMC Director Yen provided an update on construction at the SMC Malibu
  Campus.

  Commissioner Uhring asked if the City would be working with SMC or the
  County regarding changes to the emergency communications pole.

  SMC Vice President of Administration and Business Service Bonvenuto
  stated SMC was working with the City on the changes. He stated SMC was
  waiting for information from the County to move forward.

  Commissioner Uhring requested confirmation that SMC had been issued a
  certificate of occupancy but not a certificate of completion. SMC Vice
  President of Administration and Business Service Bonvenuto stated SMC
  was working through the California Division of the State Architect (DSA)
  to close the project.

  In response to Commissioner Quińones-Perez, SMC Vice President of
  Administration and Business Service Bonvenuto stated it takes time for
  DSA to issue the Certificate of Completion.

  Malibu TAC Member McClary stated the items required by the City’s
  Planning Department were separate from what DSA required.

B.  Activities at the Santa Monica College Malibu Campus
  Recommended Action: Receive an update on the opening of and current
  activities at the Santa Monica College (SMC) Malibu Campus and provide
  additional feedback on programming opportunities and events.

  SMC Noncredit and External Programs Dean Silverman stated enrollment
  for the fall semester was growing. He discussed the types of classes being
  offered.

  In response to Chair Greenstein, SMC Noncredit and External Programs
  Dean Silverman explained Counseling 20. He stated there was a 20%
  increase in enrollment from Spring 2023 to Fall 2023.

  SMC Malibu Campus Associate Dean Meyering stated Fall 2023 classes
  started last week. She stated there were over 500 students enrolled for a total
  of 28 classes, 68% of which were credit classes. She stated Emeritus
  students represented approximately 35% of enrollment. She stated the
  growth was at a sustainable rate. She stated SMC worked with the Boys and
  Girls Club of Malibu to accommodate parking for the Chili Cook-Off event
  over Labor Day weekend. She stated SMC was working with Pepperdine
  and the Audubon Society on joint offerings.

  Commissioner Quińones-Perez commended SMC Malibu Campus
  Associate Dean Meyering for her work with the Malibu community. In
  response to Commissioner Quińones-Perez, SMC Malibu Campus
  Associate Dean Meyering discussed the SMC working relationship with
  Malibu High School and recruitment from other high schools in the
  immediate area.

  Commissioner Quińones-Perez suggested working with Malibu High
  School’s PTA and boosters. Alice stated parent input was important.

  Commissioner Uhring suggested the City work with SMC to incorporate
  the Dark Sky ordinance with the Astronomy class.

  Chair Greenstein asked if the Malibu representatives had received any
  feedback from the community.

  SMC Malibu Campus Associate Dean Meyering stated the feedback from
  Malibu residents had been very positive.

  Commissioner Uhring discussed requests for film permits on the Malibu
  campus. He requested SMC abide by the City’s rules for film permits. He
  stated a member of the Arts Commission notified him of there being interest
  in renting the parking lot for a car show. He discussed issues with car shows
  in the past and requested SMC touch base with the City regarding any
  specialty permit requests.

  C.  Ongoing Role of Malibu Public Facilities Authority
  Recommended Action: Initiate a discussion on the future purposes and
  ongoing role of the Malibu Public Facilities Authority (MPFA), including a
  review of the Joint Exercise of Powers Agreement (JPA) that created the
  MPFA, and direct staff to bring back an Amendment to the JPA, if
  necessary.

  Chair Greenstein introduced the item. She stated the JPA should continue
  until all items on the project were completed.

  Commissioner Uhring and Commissioner Quińones-Perez agreed with
  Chair Greenstein.

  In response to Malibu Executive Assistant Linden, Chair Greenstein
  suggested delaying establishment of an annual meeting date until after the
  Certificate of Completion was issued. She suggested a meeting be
  scheduled in six months unless it was needed sooner.

ITEM 5  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

  Commissioner Quińones-Perez stated SMC always had faith in its
  relationship with Malibu. She stated she was glad to see what was
  accomplished.

  Commissioner Uhring agreed with Commissioner Quińones-Perez. He
  stated the City was working on recruitment and retention of employees. He
  stated he hoped the City could partner with SMC on courses to help educate
  residents on how to become involved.

  Chair Greenstein stated SMC often worked with organizations on special
  class offerings. She stated the new campus was an amazing place to take
  classes. He thanked everyone for their partnership and cooperation.

  SMC Senior Director Girard stated the next Board of Trustees meeting will
  be held in Malibu on October 3 at 7:30 p.m.

  TAC Member McClary stated the College was subject to the City’s LCPA
  for permits.

Date prepared:  August 8, 2024  Meeting date: August 14, 2024

Subject:  Santa Monica College Malibu Campus Update

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive an update on current and future class offerings
and activities at the Santa Monica College Malibu Campus and provide additional
feedback on programming opportunities and events.

DISCUSSION: The Santa Monica College Malibu campus opened its doors at the
beginning of the Spring 2023 semester. The objectives of the campus are to provide
academic excellence, lifelong learning, and community engagement. Class offerings are
spread across for-credit academic courses, noncredit career pathway courses, and self-
enrichment classes offered by Emeritus and Community Education.

The credit academic program has seen growth in the Spring 23 to Spring 24 semesters
(up 58%) and in the Fall 23 to Fall 24 semesters (up 38%). Classes are added based
primarily on student and community surveys.

Overall campus enrollment is projected to reach 625 students in Fall 2024, up from 451 in
Fall 23. Fall classes begin Monday, August 26, 2024.

A detailed report on the class offerings, together with updates on community engagement,
high school visits, and community partnerships will be presented at the meeting by the
head of the SMC Malibu Campus, Associate Dean Alice Meyering. The presentation will
be available on the MPFA website.

See https://www.smc.edu/about/campuses/malibu/ for information about the campus and
course offerings.

Date prepared:  August 8, 2024  Meeting date: August 14, 2024

Subject:  Regular Meeting Schedule

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Adopt Resolution No. MPFA 24-14, repealing Resolution
No. MPFA 17-01 and revising the regular meeting schedule.

DISCUSSION:

On February 1, 2006, the Commission adopted Resolution No. MPFA 06-01 establishing
its regular meeting schedule to meet quarterly, on the first Wednesday of each calendar
quarter, at 7:00 p.m., at Malibu City Hall, 23815 Stuart Ranch Road, in Malibu, California.
On September 6, 2017, the Commission adopted Resolution No. MPFA 17-01 to revise
the regular meeting schedule to meet on an as-needed basis, but no less than once per
calendar year.

Section 2.05 of the Joint Exercise of Powers Agreement that created the Malibu Public
Facilities Authority (Commission) states that regular meetings shall be fixed by resolution
of the Commission and that at least one regular meeting shall be held each year.

Staff recommends setting an annual regular meeting schedule to meet annually on the
first Wednesday of September at 1:00 p.m., at Malibu City Hall, 23815 Stuart Ranch
Road, in Malibu, California.

ALTERNATIVES:

Discuss and provide a recommendation on a regular annual meeting date.

  A RESOLUTION OF THE MALIBU PUBLIC FACILITIES AUTHORITY
  REPEALING RESOLUTION NO. MPFA 17-01 AND REVISING THE
  REGULAR MEETING SCHEDULE

The Commission does hereby find, order and resolve as follows:

  SECTION 1. Recitals.

  A.  On February 1, 2006, the Commission adopted Resolution No. MPFA 06-01
  establishing its regular meeting schedule to meet quarterly, on the first Wednesday
  of each calendar quarter, at 7:00 p.m., at Malibu City Hall, 23815 Stuart Ranch
  Road, in Malibu, California.

  B.  On September 6, 2017, the Commission adopted Resolution No. MPFA 17-01 to
  revise the regular meeting schedule to meet on an as-needed basis, but no less than
  once per calendar year

  C.  Section 2.05 of the Joint Exercise of Powers Agreement that created the Malibu
  Public Facilities Authority (Commission) states that regular meetings shall be fixed
  by resolution of the Commission and that at least one regular meeting shall be held
  each year.

  SECTION 2. The Commission does hereby revise its regular meeting schedule to
meet annually on the first Wednesday of September at 1:00 p.m., at Malibu City Hall, 23815
Stuart Ranch Road, in Malibu, California.

  SECTION 3. The Recording Secretary shall certify to the passage and adoption of this
resolution and enter it into the book of original resolutions.
